ov: Over 170 species of small, often brilliantly coloured frogs from the rainforests of Central and South America, active by day. Their bright colours warn predators of skin toxins taken from a diet of ants, mites and termites. Only four species are known to have been used to poison blow darts.

why.dg: The golden poison frog carries enough toxin to kill ten to twenty people, but captive-bred frogs have almost none.
why.p: Kept by hobbyists, though collecting them for the pet trade has helped threaten some wild species.

len: Often under 1.5 cm; a few up to 6 cm
rg: Tropical Central and South America, from Nicaragua to Bolivia and Brazil; introduced to Hawaii.
df: Small arthropods such as ants, mites, termites and centipedes.
fx: After the eggs hatch, a parent carries the tadpoles one at a time on its back to water, sometimes a pool inside a bromeliad.
A painkiller 200 times as potent as morphine, epibatidine, comes from the skin of one species.
